stories.title: Some universities now take 2027 applications before Class 12 exams
stories.summary: Several universities, including Flame, Ashoka, MIT WPU and WPU Goa, have opened early application rounds for their 2027 undergraduate intake, Careers360 reports. Students can apply and sit entrance assessments before their board exams. The board exams themselves remain unmoved.

stories.title: India plans 75,000 more medical seats by 2029
stories.summary: Union Health Minister JP Nadda said India will add 75,000 undergraduate and postgraduate medical seats by 2029, speaking at the HealthWealth Summit 2026. The aim is to improve medical education and widen access to healthcare. Aspiring doctors may now begin counting backwards from 2029.

stories.title: 'AI can't deliver a lamb', say students choosing hands-on careers
stories.summary: A OnePoll survey of 4,000 UK parents and their children, commissioned by Bishop Burton College, found 77 per cent of parents worry AI will hurt their child's job prospects. Two thirds are now considering vocational routes. One student summed it up with livestock.

stories.title: How to check whether a college really prepares you for AI careers
stories.summary: An Entrepreneur guide says students should ask colleges how they actually teach AI before committing. It cites PwC's 2026 Global AI Jobs Barometer, which found job ads asking for AI skills offer about 62% more pay than comparable roles. Brochures, it suggests, are not evidence.

stories.title: IIT Kanpur looks past entrance scores for cybersecurity talent
stories.summary: IIT Kanpur is pairing academic training with practical assessments to build cybersecurity skills, director Manindra Agrawal said at a briefing on its 'Greater Than Us' campaign. He named cybersecurity as one of seven technology areas critical to India.

stories.title: IIT Guwahati and Tata Electronics launch semiconductor courses
stories.summary: IIT Guwahati has teamed up with Tata Electronics on education, training and research in semiconductor assembly, testing, marking and packaging, Hindustan Times reports. The programmes will be aligned with what the industry says it needs, which is the part industry usually complains about.

stories.title: Maryland teens spend a Saturday exploring nuclear energy careers
stories.summary: About 60 ninth and 10th grade students from Southern Maryland visited Constellation's Calvert Cliffs Clean Energy Center for its first Energy Exploration Day. The one-day workshop covered the science of energy production and introduced students to engineers and skilled trades workers.

stories.title: A community college opens a SparkLab for teen tech careers
stories.summary: Fayetteville Technical Community College in North Carolina has opened a SparkLab where middle and high school students can build skills for cybersecurity and tech jobs. It is the first SparkNC site on a community college campus, WKML reports.

stories.title: Yeshiva University offers graduate school places to high school applicants
stories.summary: Yeshiva University has launched YU Direct, which lets qualified high school applicants secure early admission to select graduate programmes at the same time as they are admitted as undergraduates. The idea is to plan the master's before the first lecture.

stories.title: A college principal makes the case for T Levels
stories.summary: Lisa Capper, principal of Sandwell College, writes that T Levels and vocational education are vital to the Black Country and Birmingham region. She notes that this autumn some young people continued academic study while others chose technical routes or apprenticeships.

stories.title: A 12-year-old builds an AI tool that forecasts earthquake aftershocks
stories.summary: Bowen Wang, a Class 7 student at Central Middle School in San Carlos, California, built Aftershock Oracle, an AI tool that estimates the quakes that follow a big earthquake, and won a national technology award. Predicting the first quake remains unsolved, so he started with the second.

stories.title: A Delhi Class 12 student's eye-screening kit reaches 22,500 people
stories.summary: Aditya Gupta of Springdales School, Dhaula Kuan, built NetraKit, a low-cost 3D-printed device for preliminary vision screening, after volunteering with the National Association for the Blind. It has reportedly reached nearly 22,500 people through community health camps and nonprofit programmes.

stories.title: A seventh grader tests plant gels that soak up microplastics
stories.summary: Isabella Garry from Eden Prairie, Minnesota, tested whether gels made from common plants could absorb microplastics in a lab model of the stomach. Her gels removed up to 93.3% in simulated stomach fluid, and she was named a finalist in the Thermo Fisher Junior Innovators Challenge.

stories.title: A bomb-defusing robot and cheap smart glasses win the Viksit Bharat Buildathon
stories.summary: Ten school student teams from states including Assam, Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Gujarat were named national winners of the Viksit Bharat Buildathon 2025. Projects included a spider-shaped bomb-defusing robot, an instant flask, an urban breathing pole and bone-conduction smart glasses.

stories.title: Coimbatore government school students send a research payload skyward
stories.summary: Students from 11 government middle schools in Periyanaickenpalayam block designed, built and launched an atmospheric research payload on a helium balloon. It studied airborne particulate matter and conditions at different altitudes. Homework, for once, went up rather than in.

stories.title: A 14-year-old violinist uses Python to explain expressive playing
stories.summary: Seiji Iigaya from Tenafly, New Jersey, won the 2026 Thermo Fisher Scientific Junior Innovators Challenge and a $3,500 stipend for using code to model the physics of expressive violin playing. Practice, it turns out, can also be computed.

stories.title: A 17-year-old Delhi student takes startup lessons into classrooms
stories.summary: Arjit Aggarwal, who watched his father build two companies into unicorns, now runs entrepreneurship workshops and camps in schools, News9 reports. His programmes have reportedly reached nearly 700 students in Uttarakhand and about 1,200 in Gujarat. The family business, it seems, now includes the curriculum.

stories.title: An Ilkley sixth former wins the first Alan Bennett Prize
stories.summary: Maya Robinson-Bakes of Ilkley Grammar School has won the inaugural Alan Bennett Prize, launched by the Rotary Club of Ilkley. Sixth formers were invited to write a 1,000-word story, inspired by the Yorkshire playwright and novelist.

stories.title: A Year 6 student wins Australia's national poetry slam with a poem about AI
stories.summary: Twelve-year-old Blake Mackenzie of Tighes Hill Public School won the youth final of the Australian Poetry Slam at the Sydney Opera House, months after writing his first poem. He was the youngest of 16 finalists. The poem was about AI, and AI did not write it.

stories.title: A Naperville student wins a state music composition prize
stories.summary: Chloe Ma of Naperville Central High School has won the Music Teachers National Association State Senior Composition Competition for 2026. She has studied music for more than a decade, starting with piano lessons.

stories.title: ISRO puts the NVS-03 navigation satellite into orbit
stories.summary: The GSLV-F18 lifted off from Sriharikota on 30 October and placed the NVS-03 satellite into its intended geosynchronous transfer orbit 18 minutes later, ISRO said. The satellite strengthens NavIC, India's own navigation system, so the phone may soon have options.

stories.title: Meet the 'hell chicken', the first known fruit-eating dinosaur
stories.summary: Researchers have identified Infernogallus jamesi, a toothless, turkey-sized dinosaur with a parrot-like skull built for eating fruit, The Independent reports. It is the first documented frugivorous dinosaur. Its name suggests a fiercer diet than it had.

stories.title: 17,346 rooibos seeds are heading to space
stories.summary: More than 17,000 South African rooibos seeds have begun their trip to the United States ahead of a mission to the International Space Station, where they will be exposed to conditions beyond Earth. It is a first-of-its-kind experiment for the indigenous tea plant.

stories.title: You can send your name to Titan
stories.summary: NASA has opened an online registry for its Dragonfly mission to Saturn's moon Titan. Names will go on a microchip aboard the rotorcraft, which is scheduled to launch no earlier than July 2028. Signees get a digital boarding pass, though no window seat.

stories.title: Webb photographs a Cat's Head Nebula in time for Halloween
stories.summary: NASA released a mid-infrared view from the James Webb Space Telescope of the Cat's Head Nebula on 29 October. The shape was likely sculpted by ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula. The timing was purely astronomical, presumably.

stories.title: Voyager 1 goes quiet, then calls home
stories.summary: NASA confirmed on 29 October that Voyager 1 is back in contact after an unexpected interruption, though questions remain about what caused it. Launched in September 1977, it has travelled farther than any other human-made spacecraft. Commands take many hours to reach it.

stories.title: A survey finds over 2,000 new galaxies in the Virgo cluster
stories.summary: A new survey of the Virgo cluster, about 54 million light-years away, has more than doubled the number of galaxies known in it, IFLScience reports. Some are millions of times fainter than previously known galaxies. The neighbourhood was busier than anyone had noticed.

stories.title: Archaeologists may have found the oldest shipwreck ever
stories.summary: A shipwreck near Turkey's Kekova Island could date back to when some of Egypt's pyramids were built, CBC Kids News reports. The wooden ship is long gone, but its stone anchors and amphoras remain. The pottery matches Egyptian jars from about 4,700 years ago.

stories.title: A rock found in Mali turns out to be 4.1 billion years old and from Mars
stories.summary: Prospectors found the rose-tinted meteorite in Mali in 2022, and experts first took it for a common Martian rock. NASA-funded researchers now say Teghaza 001 is a fragment of the primordial Martian crust, altered by water about 4.1 billion years ago.

stories.title: Five flowers new to science were described in India this year
stories.summary: The Better India rounds up five flowering plants formally described in 2026, including Crotalaria phulei from Nagpur district, named after Savitribai Phule, and Parakaempferia alba from Arunachal Pradesh. A plant only counts as new once researchers publish the comparison.

stories.title: The helmethead sea muppet is not a seahorse
stories.summary: Researchers have named a new thumb-sized fish from deep reefs off southern Australia, the helmethead sea muppet, Australyichthys aegis. It looks like a seahorse but belongs to a different group of fish entirely. Its name was clearly the easy part.

stories.title: Four new frog species are named in Peru
stories.summary: FIU biologist Alessandro Catenazzi and colleagues used body shape, calls and genetic evidence to describe four new Oreobates frogs collected near Cordillera Azul National Park in Peru. As the university notes, science cannot study a species until people know it exists.

stories.title: NASA asks industry whether Hubble can be serviced again
stories.summary: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center has issued a request for information on ways to service the Hubble Space Telescope or dispose of it safely. Hubble launched in April 1990 and has worked for 36 years.

stories.title: Daily temperature swings change how alligators become male or female
stories.summary: In alligator nests, temperature decides whether a hatchling is male or female. A University of Georgia experiment found eggs exposed to daily swings produced females at a lower average temperature than lab rules predict, which could change climate forecasts for the species.

stories.title: Venus may have swallowed its own moon
stories.summary: Computer simulations by astrophysicist Stephen Kane of UC Riverside suggest Venus's slow spin and gravity could have pulled a moon down onto the planet. The study, in The Astrophysical Journal, does not establish that Venus ever had a moon.

stories.title: Old radio recordings reveal 51 hidden pulsars
stories.summary: Astronomers reanalysing archival data from the Green Bank survey with more powerful algorithms have found 51 new pulsars, including one spinning every 3.2 milliseconds. The signals had been buried in noise for years. Old data, it seems, rewards a second look.

stories.title: How to walk into your mocks with more confidence
stories.summary: BBC Bitesize asked teacher Tommy T for tips on mock GCSEs. He says mocks are a chance to practise time management, handle nerves and understand papers before the summer, and can be used to build confidence as well as spot gaps.

stories.title: Test anxiety starts long before the test, say psychologists
stories.summary: Writing in Education Week, psychologists who treat test anxiety say they have reassuring news as in-class exams and the SAT return. Students can feel anxious during tests and still perform, they argue, and the real work happens well before exam day.

stories.title: A student asks who teaches us to rest
stories.summary: A student at Staples High School writes about co-founding a Yoga and Wellness Club after noticing classmates stressed and overwhelmed. An English teacher pitched the idea. School teaches hard work thoroughly, the piece notes, and breathing less so.

stories.title: CBSE Class 10 maths: basic and standard sample papers compared
stories.summary: An EdexLive analysis of the 2026 to 27 sample papers for Mathematics Basic and Mathematics Standard finds both follow the same exam structure, while the questions differ in how much application and reasoning they demand. Useful for planning revision either way.

stories.title: A Pune coach on the final stretch before JEE Main 2027
stories.summary: Lalit Kumar, founder of Prime Academy Pune, advises JEE Main 2027 candidates to stop counting chapters and start counting marks in the last weeks. The column pictures a student at night doing frightening arithmetic with too many chapters and too few days.

stories.title: What happens if you missed grade 4 in GCSE English
stories.summary: Students who finished Year 11 in 2026 without a grade 4 in English keep studying it until 18. A grade 3 means working towards a resit, while grade 2 or below can mean Functional Skills level 2. About 700 Solihull pupils are in this position.

stories.title: Common mistakes to avoid on the JEE Main 2027 form
stories.summary: About 10,000 aspirants completed initial JEE Main 2027 registration steps in the first few days, Allen reports, and experts urge candidates to move cautiously. Rushing the form often leads to mistakes that are tedious to fix later.

stories.title: An 11-year-old wins the Arab Reading Challenge and plans a school library
stories.summary: Mayar Mohammed from Egypt won the Arab Reading Challenge in Dubai, reading more than 60 books during the competition. She received 500,000 dirhams and said she will spend it on a library for her school. The prize for reading is more reading.

stories.title: Math Kangaroo 2027 runs from 17 to 30 April
stories.summary: The Mathematical Kangaroo Competition 2027 will be held between 17 April and 30 April 2027 for students in Grades 1 to 12, PW reports. Students should check the announced dates and complete registration before the deadline.

stories.title: Nigerian school debaters share ₦2.2 million in prizes
stories.summary: Arewa Radio awarded ₦2.2 million to winners of the third season of its Muhawwara school debate competition in Northern Nigeria. Thirty-two students from 16 schools competed over three weeks, and Elmar International School came first with 41.5 marks.

stories.title: Over 9,000 Malaysian secondary students take part in an AI hackathon
stories.summary: The AI Muda@NADI Hackathon 2026, run with CelcomDigi through Malaysia's National Information Dissemination Centres, drew more than 9,000 secondary students. Twenty-six teams reached the national finals with AI solutions to real-world problems.

stories.title: A writing competition opens for high school seniors in South Carolina
stories.summary: Wellmore of Lexington has opened its annual Silver Pen Competition for local high school seniors. Students submit original essays, and residents of the retirement community serve as judges. It has connected generations through storytelling since 2012.

stories.title: Shiv Nadar School hosts the ISSO National Fencing Championship
stories.summary: The International Schools Sports Organisation held its 8th National Fencing Championship at Shiv Nadar School, Faridabad, with fencers from 44 schools competing in Under-14, Under-17 and older age groups over two days.

stories.title: Two middle schoolers win a Pennsylvania school bus safety poster contest
stories.summary: Two Bald Eagle Middle School students were honoured for their school bus safety posters during School Bus Safety Week. The state Department of Transportation and State Police presented certificates and trophies at a ceremony in Hershey.

stories.title: KLU students win at the Rashtriya Innovation Challenge in Guntur
stories.summary: Student teams from Koneru Lakshmaiah Education Foundation won awards in two categories at the Guntur district level of the Rashtriya Innovation Challenge 2026, run by the Andhra Pradesh government with the Ratan Tata Innovation Hub. Each team won ₹10,000.

stories.title: Marwadi University launches a Kiran Bedi scholarship for girls
stories.summary: Marwadi University in Gujarat has announced a scholarship named after Kiran Bedi, India's first woman IPS officer, to support meritorious girl students in higher education. It was announced during her campus visit.

stories.title: A national scholarship exam opens for Classes 4 to 12
stories.summary: The Dr. A.P.J. Abdul Kalam Welfare Society has announced the All India Bright Student Award Scholarship Exam 2026, also called Bright Student X. The national exam aims to identify and reward talented students from Classes 4 to 12.

stories.title: FFE opens scholarships for first-year engineering, medical and law students
stories.summary: The Foundation for Excellence has invited applications for its 2026 to 27 programme for first-year Engineering, MBBS and Law students across India. Selected students receive ₹50,000 or more based on merit and financial need. Applications are through ffe.org.

stories.title: Barry University's Stamps Scholars cover four years in full
stories.summary: Barry University in the US is accepting applications for its Stamps Scholars Program 2027, open to students worldwide. It covers tuition, accommodation, meals, books and transport for four years, plus a $6,000 enrichment award.

stories.title: York University's Panther Promise covers full tuition
stories.summary: York University in Nebraska will cover full tuition for eligible incoming undergraduates from 2027 to 28 through grants, scholarships and university support. Students must qualify for a Federal Pell Grant and meet household income guidelines.

stories.title: A Canadian mine funds four years of study for Indigenous Grade 12 students
stories.summary: Artemis Gold and Steven Dean have launched the Blackwater Dean Family Indigenous Award in mining. From 2027 it will fund four years of post-secondary study in mining-related fields for up to five Indigenous Grade 12 students a year.

stories.title: A Nigerian student lands a fully funded scholarship in Korea
stories.summary: A Nigerian student named Pella documented her route from filling scholarship forms during exhausting night classes to studying in South Korea, Tuko reports. She called the application process draining. The vlog's before and after shots do the rest.

stories.title: ASPRS opens 2027 scholarships and a $25,000 research grant
stories.summary: The American Society for Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing and its foundation have announced 2027 scholarships and a $25,000 geospatial science research grant for undergraduates, postgraduates and early-career professionals. The 2027 cycle includes 12 student scholarships worth a combined $61,800.

stories.title: Spain asks Moroccan students to return €7.88 million in scholarships
stories.summary: Spain's Education Ministry has demanded repayment of €446.2 million in grants awarded over eight academic years, including €33.6 million from foreign students, Morocco World News reports. Moroccan students top the foreign list at €7.88 million.

stories.title: JEE Main 2027 Session 1 applications close on 22 November
stories.summary: The National Testing Agency is running JEE Main 2027 Session 1 registration from 24 October to 22 November 2026. Candidates should check the information bulletin for eligibility, syllabus and fees before applying.

stories.title: CBSE drops the AI and computational thinking modules for this Class 9 batch
stories.summary: CBSE has dropped three curricular components, including the computational thinking and AI modules, for current Class 9 students. The move came six days after NCERT released its introductory CT and AI module on 23 October.

stories.title: Six CBSE clarifications in seven months
stories.summary: India Today counts at least six major rounds of CBSE clarifications since May 2026, covering digital evaluation, extra marks, the three-language policy, passing criteria and curriculum. The latest came on 29 October. Students are advised to keep reading the circulars.

stories.title: CBSE has not yet released the 2027 board exam timetable
stories.summary: The List of Candidates deadline has passed, and Class 10 and 12 students are still waiting for CBSE's tentative 2027 date sheet, India Today reports. Last year the board released it in September. It is now nearly November.

stories.title: Karnataka releases its 2nd PUC 2027 timetable
stories.summary: KSEAB has released the final timetable for the 2027 Second Pre-University Course exams, which will run in two sessions with exam 1 starting on 27 February, India Today reports. Students can now check subject dates and timings.

stories.title: The IB is booming in Australia
stories.summary: A record 3,100 students in Australia are sitting this year's International Baccalaureate diploma exams, part of a 22 per cent rise in IB offerings over a decade, the AFR reports. Unlike the standard Year 12 route, there is nowhere to hide in the IB.

stories.title: Today's SAT has shorter passages and fewer vocabulary questions than in the 1980s
stories.summary: A Johns Hopkins Institute for Education Policy study, sponsored by Thomas Aquinas College, found the SAT reading section now uses shorter passages and less vocabulary than 40 years ago. Students may have noticed anyway.

stories.title: South Korea will prosecute students who cheated with smart glasses
stories.summary: South Korea will file criminal complaints against students caught cheating on the national university entrance exam with smart glasses and will toughen penalties, an official told AFP. The glasses can take photos and talk to an AI assistant.

stories.title: CLAT 2027 registration closes on 31 October
stories.summary: The Consortium of National Law Universities closes the CLAT 2027 registration portal on 31 October 2026. The window has been open since 3 August. That is nearly three months of time, now down to the last day.

stories.title: SRMJEEE 2027 will run in two phases
stories.summary: SRM Institute of Science and Technology will hold SRMJEEE 2027 phase 1 on 17 and 18 April and phase 2 on 19 and 20 June for BTech admissions, Careers360 reports. Application forms open soon.

stories.title: 21.47% of students earn top grade in Taiwan's English listening test
stories.summary: Taiwan's first Test of English Listening Comprehension for the 2027 academic year saw 21.47% of students earn the top grade, down from 22.59% a year earlier. A total of 90,914 students registered, and the absentee rate was 3.6%.

stories.title: Over a million Kenyan candidates begin KCSE written papers on 2 November
stories.summary: Education Cabinet Secretary Julius Migos Ogamba said this week's national assessments went smoothly as 1,048,355 candidates prepare to start the Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education written exams on Monday, 2 November 2026.

stories.title: Australia expands biometric checks for visa applicants in India
stories.summary: Since 26 October 2026, Australian visa applicants in India may be asked for fingerprints and a facial image, The Indian Express reports. The expansion covers nearly 60 countries. Indian students heading to Australia should plan for the extra step.

stories.title: What the India and New Zealand trade deal means for students
stories.summary: The India and New Zealand Free Trade Agreement came into force on 20 October 2026. Alongside tariff cuts, it brings new visa categories, longer post-study work rights for some graduates and a working holiday scheme for young Indians.

stories.title: Australia consults on a student visa overhaul
stories.summary: Australia's Home Affairs department has opened consultation on revising the Genuine Student requirement, including a possible rule that applicants hold study funds in Australian bank accounts. The government says it wants more certainty for genuine students and tighter financial checks.

stories.title: Post-study jobs now shape Indian students' choice of country
stories.summary: IDP Education's latest Emerging Futures report, based on more than 4,800 students in 106 countries and regions, finds Indian students still prioritise overseas education despite visa uncertainty, with employment prospects increasingly deciding where they go.

stories.title: International students who struggle with health understand their cover least
stories.summary: Research by Medibank and Nous Group found one in four international students in Australia struggle with health and wellbeing. Those in the poorest wellbeing groups knew least about available services and their insurance.

stories.title: English UK reviews student protection after school closures
stories.summary: English UK is consulting providers, agents and students on what protection students should get when an accredited English language school closes suddenly. Chief executive Jodie Gray said recent closures 'sent shockwaves across international education'.

stories.title: Two UK English schools close, leaving hundreds of students to find new ones
stories.summary: Two English language training providers in the UK have closed in succession, forcing hundreds of international students to change plans. Those who already paid tuition and accommodation are waiting to learn how their money will be handled.

stories.title: South Korea will deport foreign students caught working as delivery riders
stories.summary: South Korea is stepping up crackdowns on foreign nationals working illegally as delivery riders, and international students caught in restricted sectors will face forced deportation, the Ministry of Justice said. Student visas, it is reminding everyone, are for studying.

stories.title: What exchange programmes offer high school students
stories.summary: The Daily Star looks at international exchange programmes for high school students, from Japan to the United States. It argues they offer cultural immersion, independence and new perspectives that virtual connections cannot quite match.

stories.title: Master's students give their reasons for studying abroad
stories.summary: GMAC asked international master's students why they studied abroad. Their answers include new skills, alternate career paths and lifelong friends, and the piece notes that subject, cost and location all weigh on where to go.

stories.title: Indiana students help make coding accessible for blind learners
stories.summary: Microsoft MakeCode's drag and drop block editor is a friendly start to coding, but not for students who cannot see. Shawn Humphrey, a teacher at the Indiana School for the Blind and Visually Impaired, says new research has changed that.

stories.title: China's 'super students' would rather not be called that
stories.summary: Ninth grader Zhang Shaoqing builds tools with AI, but told China Daily the 'super student' label feels like pressure, as if he is not a good student unless he has built something. He would rather be seen as an ordinary student who stayed passionate about one field.

stories.title: Tangible Africa's unplugged coding reaches classrooms worldwide
stories.summary: Professor Jean Greyling of Nelson Mandela University described how Tangible Africa, which teaches coding without computers, grew from an honours project into an international movement. He spoke at the Universities South Africa higher education conference.

stories.title: Busan will open Korea's first 'physical AI research schools'
stories.summary: Busan's education office will designate five physical AI research schools from next year, the first in South Korea. The aim is to go beyond basic coding so students think independently, discuss and solve problems. A workshop for 300 teachers is set for Monday.

stories.title: Malaysia's push for AI in classrooms meets a reality check
stories.summary: As Malaysia speeds up AI use in schools, the SCMP reports fears that students will trade understanding for easy answers. One Kuala Lumpur father taught his eight-year-old a few prompts and checks the answers closely. The checking may be the lesson.

stories.title: A Palo Alto school uses AI for academics, then takes it away
stories.summary: Alpha School in Palo Alto, one of 40 in the US, shapes each student's lesson plan with AI, and children study maths and science for two hours a day. Co-founder Mackenzie Price says that frees the rest of the day for social skills.

stories.title: Qweebi raises $500,000 to expand STEM and robotics learning
stories.summary: K-12 edtech startup Qweebi, now in more than 5,200 US schools, has raised $500,000 in a round led by Inflection Point Ventures. It will use the money to improve its digital learning platform and expand.

stories.title: Bhonsala Military School students see drones and robotics at MCEME
stories.summary: Sixty Class 12 students from Bhonsala Military School, Nashik, visited the Military College of Electronics and Mechanical Engineering in Secunderabad on 29 October. The tour introduced them to the Army's technical training and emerging technologies such as drones, AI and robotics.

stories.title: Is Nepal's school system ready for AI?
stories.summary: A Khabarhub opinion piece says Nepali students can now use AI to understand science, practise languages and get writing feedback in seconds. It asks whether a system long built on textbooks and prescribed curricula is ready to make use of it.

stories.title: A Kansas district asks a work group to write its student AI policy
stories.summary: Shawnee Mission schools have formed a work group to recommend a student AI policy. Math teacher Jill Johnson says she can tell when students use AI on homework because their working does not match how the class practised it.

stories.title: Highland School District sets out AI guidelines
stories.summary: Highland School District's board approved an AI policy framework in September, setting out how students and teachers may use the technology while keeping academic integrity and independent learning, Times-Tribune News reports.

stories.title: Robotics mini-grants let 160 Columbia Gorge students compete for free
stories.summary: Robotics mini-grants from the Gorge Technology Alliance and Columbia Gorge STEM Hub, now in their fourth year, cover team registration, hardware and materials so over 160 young people in Oregon and Washington can build, code and compete at no cost.

stories.title: Digital Science buys Jenni AI, a research writing tool
stories.summary: Digital Science has acquired Jenni AI, which says more than 8 million students and researchers in 189 countries use it to find sources, draft and check citations. It pitches itself as built for research, unlike general-purpose AI tools.

stories.title: Scale AI and UMSL launch an AI course for K-12 teachers
stories.summary: Scale, the University of Missouri St. Louis and Lindbergh Schools launched Fundamentals of AI for Educators, a 12-hour self-paced course and microcredential to help K-12 teachers use AI effectively and ethically. It is available nationwide.

stories.title: Morocco's 'Route 250' robotics caravan will train teachers nationwide
stories.summary: Morocco's education ministry, the US Embassy and LOOP for Science and Technology launched the Route 250 robotics caravan in Rabat on 27 October. It will visit all 12 regional academies to build primary and middle school teachers' digital, coding and robotics skills.

stories.title: Georgia teachers bring nanotechnology research back to class
stories.summary: Two Georgia high school teachers spent the summer working with Georgia Tech nanotechnology researchers. Robin Osborn, who teaches ecology at Meadowcreek High, says she had to take her own advice about working through frustration in science.

stories.title: A Surrey teacher wins a national award for forest kindergarten
stories.summary: Kindergarten teacher Ellen Petersson's class has spent part of every school day in the forest for six years, rain or snow. She has won the Susan Langley Earth Steward Teaching Award, a national Canadian honour, for daily outdoor lessons that use pinecones for maths and insects for science.

stories.title: Teacher trainees must now teach five to eight adults to read
stories.summary: New Centre guidelines require student teachers in recognised programmes to help five to eight non-literate adults gain literacy and certification. Trainees earn academic credits based on how many learners they get certified.

stories.title: UNESCO's GlobALE curriculum trains youth and adult educators
stories.summary: UNESCO's GlobALE curriculum supports educators who teach young people and adults basic skills in Latin America, with intercultural understanding and popular education at its centre. Teaching approaches, it says, should reflect the communities they serve.

stories.title: How schools build career partnerships with real industry
stories.summary: Education Week looks at Lakota schools near Cincinnati, whose Cyber Academy has run for seven years with cybersecurity classes, certifications and mentoring from industry professionals. The district gets no state or federal funding for the programme.

stories.title: What should change after the Supreme Court's ruling on children and the internet
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has held that children have a fundamental right to access and use the internet, under Articles 21 and 19(1)(a). A Hindu piece looks at what schools, parents and policymakers must now change.

stories.title: NCTE forms committees to revise teacher recruitment rules
stories.summary: The National Council for Teacher Education has formed two expert groups to review teacher recruitment rules and CTET and STET eligibility. The move aims to make four-year ITEP graduates eligible for school teaching jobs.

stories.title: Parents pay £42,000 in fees, then the school closes
stories.summary: Leweston School near Sherborne in Dorset, which taught pupils from nursery to 18, is the latest private school to announce closure since VAT on fees began in January 2025, the i reports. The century-old school gave no reason.

stories.title: India will need over a billion sq ft of new private education space by FY35
stories.summary: A CBRE report estimates India will need 1 to 1.5 billion sq ft of additional private education infrastructure by FY2035, driven by rising enrolment and demand for quality education. Private K-12 schools are expected to lead.

stories.title: Bangladesh links climate and education data to protect learning
stories.summary: Bangladesh is integrating climate, disaster and education data so schools can better withstand floods, cyclones and heatwaves. Officials say the information is currently fragmented across institutions, making vulnerable schools hard to identify.

stories.title: Bihar orders 75% attendance and no police housing in model schools
stories.summary: Bihar's education department has told officials to enforce 75% attendance at Saraswati Vidya Niketan model schools, avoid using them as exam centres and, as far as possible, stop police personnel from being housed in them.

stories.title: Karnataka opens LKG and UKG classes in 581 government schools
stories.summary: Karnataka has permitted separate pre-primary classes in 581 government schools for 2026 to 27 under Samagra Shiksha Karnataka, Careers360 reports. Classes will run from 10 am to 3:30 pm and follow a bilingual, activity-based approach with Balachaitanya activity books.

stories.title: Himachal approves 3,100 teachers for its CBSE schools
stories.summary: The Himachal Pradesh government has approved engaging 3,100 teachers across subjects in its CBSE-affiliated government schools, including 600 for professional English and maths, ET Education reports. Of those, 240 will teach English and 360 mathematics, and another 2,500 will work on a fixed honorarium.

stories.title: Telangana orders daily special classes before SSC exams
stories.summary: With March 2027 SSC exams approaching, Telangana's School Education Department has told government schools to run daily special classes, regular tests and individual mentoring, and to finish the syllabus on time.

stories.title: Only 61 Nagaland schools offer science, says the NBSE chairman
stories.summary: Nagaland Board of School Education chairman Rangumbuing Nsarangbe said only 61 schools in 14 districts offer the science stream and called for wider science education. He spoke while inaugurating a science lab block in Dimapur.

stories.title: NEP 2020 at six years, from the classroom
stories.summary: A Tribune viewpoint looks at the National Education Policy six years on. It credits the flexible 5+3+3+4 structure and focus on foundational literacy and numeracy, and examines how the shift from rote learning is going on the ground.

stories.title: Pralhad Joshi calls for focused execution of NEP 2020
stories.summary: Union Minister Pralhad Joshi called for effective implementation of the National Education Policy 2020 while inaugurating a new academic building at NIEPA in New Delhi. He described the policy as a comprehensive reform.

stories.title: Tamil Nadu declares 9 November a school holiday after Diwali
stories.summary: Tamil Nadu has declared Monday 9 November a holiday for schools and colleges because Diwali falls on Sunday 8 November. To make up for it, Saturday 28 November will be a working day. The holiday, in other words, is on loan.
